record.paper_title: NLS ground states on metric trees: existence results and open questions
record.context_brief: Positivity of the non-radial threshold mass for p in (2,4)
record.original_question: For the nonlinear Schrödinger energy E(u,G) = (1/2)∫_G |u′|² dx − (1/p)∫_G |u|^p dx on the rooted binary metric tree T_o or the unrooted binary metric tree T, with exponent p in (2,4), mass μ > 0, mass-constrained space H^1_μ(G) = {u in H^1(G): ∫_G |u|² dx = μ}, ground-state energy L_G(μ) = inf_{u in H^1_μ(G)} E(u,G), best Poincaré constant λ_1, and threshold μ_G^* = max{μ ≥ 0: L_G(μ) = (1/2)λ_1 μ}, is μ_G^* strictly positive?

evidence.quote: Given a metric graph G, a number p ∈ (2,6) and a mass μ > 0, the ‘ground state problem’ on G is the minimization problem min_{u∈H^1_μ(G)} E(u,G), where E(u,G) is as in (1) and H^1_μ(G) is the class of mass-constrained functions H^1_μ(G) := {u ∈ H^1(G) : ∫_G |u|^2 dx = μ}.
Assume G = T (or G = T_o) and p ∈ (2,6), and define μ_G^* := max { μ ≥ 0 : L_G(μ) = 1/2 λ_1 μ }.

Remark 1.3. When p ∈ (2,4) we are not able to prove that μ_G^* > 0: if, as we believe, this was the case, then at μ = μ_G^* a transition would occur from nonexistence to existence of ground states (exactly as when p ∈ [4,6)), while, if μ_G^* = 0, then ground states would exist for every mass.

artifact.category_tag: NLS ground states on metric graphs
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let T be the infinite unrooted binary metric tree, namely the metric graph obtained by gluing copies of the half-line so that every vertex has degree 3, and let T_o be the rooted infinite binary metric tree, where one distinguished vertex (the root) has degree 2 and every other vertex has degree 3 (all edges have length 1, say, or any fixed positive length, and the resulting graph is endowed with the natural metric and Lebesgue measure on each edge). For G ∈ {T, T_o}, let H^1(G) denote the usual Sobolev space of continuous functions on G whose restriction to each edge belongs to H^1, and define, for μ > 0, the mass-constrained space
   H^1_μ(G) := { u ∈ H^1(G) : ∫_G |u|^2 dx = μ }.
For p ∈ (2,4), define the NLS energy
   E(u, G) := (1/2) ∫_G |u'|^2 dx − (1/p) ∫_G |u|^p dx,
and the ground-state level
   L_G(μ) := inf_{u ∈ H^1_μ(G)} E(u, G).
Let
   λ_1 := inf_{u ∈ H^1(G), u ≠ 0} (∫_G |u'|^2 dx) / (∫_G |u|^2 dx)
denote the best Poincaré constant of G (which is strictly positive for both T and T_o), and define the threshold mass
   μ_G^* := max{ μ ≥ 0 : L_G(μ) = (1/2) λ_1 μ }.
Prove or disprove that μ_G^* > 0.
artifact.status_search_result: The published version of the work introducing this threshold (J. London Math. Soc., 2020) lists μ_G^* > 0 for p ∈ (2,4) as an open question, while it is established for p ∈ [4,6). A search of subsequent literature on NLS ground states on metric trees and graphs did not turn up a definitive resolution of this specific subcritical positivity question; the status appears to remain open, but no conclusive confirmation either way was found.

status_evidence.snippet: When p ∈ (2,4) we are not able to prove that μ_G^* > 0.
status_evidence.claim: The positivity of μ_G^* in the range p ∈ (2,4) is stated as an open question.

status_evidence.title: NLS ground states on metric trees - Journal of the London Mathematical Society
status_evidence.snippet: Considers minimization of the NLS energy on a metric tree, with several open questions concerning threshold phenomena.
status_evidence.claim: Threshold phenomena for ground states on metric trees include unresolved cases in the subcritical regime.
